Chief Complaint:

Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:

History of Present Illness:
Patient is a ___ yo woman with h/o hypertension, morbid obesity, 
PCOS, pulmonary embolism in ___ ?due to OCP, who presents from 
clinic with progressive shortness of breath and DOE. Patient 
says the symptoms started about one month prior to this with 
cough and increasing DOE. Over the last four to five days, she 
has developed increasing cough with sputum production in the 
morning, associated with low grade fevers up to 100 as measured 
at home. In addition, she has had muscle and joint pain in her 
neck, back, shoulders and wrists. She denies rash. There is no 
recent travel history or sick contacts. She lives alone in an 
apartment in ___ but is in frequent contact with children via 
her mother, who takes care of several children, ages ranging 
from 2 months to ___ years.

Of note, she was admitted to ___ one month ago for pneumonia. 
She received cefpodoxime and azithromycin during that admission 
for presumptive community-acquired pneumonia. Prior to the 
current admission, she had CTA chest to evaluate for PE. The 
study showed no PE; however, there were diffuse multifocal areas 
of ground-glass opacity noted in both lungs, left more than 
right, with pleural thickening in both lung apices. There was 
also note of bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, concerning for 
sarcoid. She has had recent ACE levels checked which were 
normal. Her HIV status, per her report is negative in ___ 
___ and she has had no high-risk exposure since then.

In the ED today, vitals were 101, 130, 145/58, 20, and 98% RA. 
CXR showed worsening ground-glass opacity of the left lower 
lobe. Patient was given levofloxacin and 2L normal saline and 
admitted for further evaluation.
 
Past Medical History:

in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery suspicious for PE in 
___. S/p treatment with coumadin.

contraceptive.

Imaging Studies:

CTA chest (___):
1. Negative for central pulmonary embolism.  
2. Diffuse ground-glass opacities could represent infection, 
hemorrage/vasculitis or drug reaction (Is the patient IV drug 
abuser???). 
The association with lymphadenopathy rises the possibility of

Transbronquial biopsy and comparison with the prior studies 
would be helpful.  
3. Thickening of the anterior wall of the esophagus at the EG 
junction 
warrants evaluation with endoscopy.

CXR (___):
Worsening ground-glass opacity of the left lower lobe which may 
indicate a progression of disease although given the short 
interval since the prior study this simply may represent 
difference in modality representation.
 
Brief Hospital Course:
A ___ year-old woman with past medical history of pulmonary 
embolism (believed secondary to oral contraceptives), morbid 
obesity, and hypertension, now presents from clinic with 
progressive DOE and fevers to 101.

# FEVERS, COUGH, HYPOXIA: Differential included infectious 
causes such as CAP, viral pneumonia, influenza, viral bronchitis 
versus non-infectious causes such as sarcoid or vasculitis. 
Pulmonary service was consulted and felt that the bilateral 
infiltrates were consistent with acute infectious process, 
possibly superimposed on underlying lung disease such as 
sarcoid. They agreed with plan to treat with ceftriaxone and 
azithromycin. They recommended to hold off bronchoscopy if her 
symptoms improved with antibiotics, as bronchoscopy would likely 
require general anesthesia and trip to OR given her body 
habitus. Infectious labs were sent, including viral culture, 
influenza DFA, urine Legionella, and blood/urine cultures. 
Unfortunately no infectious agent was isolated. In addition, 
___, RF, and ANCA were sent and all were negative. Her symptoms 
continued to improve on antibiotics, with improving oxygenation, 
decreasing tachycardia, and no fevers for several days prior to 
discharge. She was still having difficulty maintaining oxygen 
sats in ___ during ambulation, and therefore we decided to 
discharge her with home oxygen (for exertion) as she recovers 
from this infection. She will follow-up in pulmonary clinic in 
one month and will undergo repeat CT and PFT testing on that 
date. If there is not complete resolution of the infiltrates, 
she may need bronchoscopy at some point in the future. She is 
discharged to complete a 14-day course of cefpodoxime (she 
finished a five-day course of azithromycin in the hospital).

# ESOPHAGEAL THICKENING / REFLUX DISEASE / ASPIRATION RISK: 
Pulmonary team felt that she was at increased risk of aspiration 
given obese body habitus and symptoms of GERD. We therefore 
started a PPI at twice daily dosing. She may benefit from 
esophageal biopsy in the future.

# TACHYCARDIA: She had sinus tachycardia (confirmed on EKG) up 
to 140s during ambulation. This was felt to be due to pulmonary 
infection. Initially she was bolused with IVF, and as her 
infection was treated, the tachycardia improved. At time of 
discharge, her heart rate at rest is 90-100 with sinus tach of 
120-130 during ambulation.

# HYPERTENSION: This was well-controlled. At times her systolic 
pressure was on the low end of normal (low 100s) and her HCTZ 
was held.

# OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA: She may benefit from sleep study as 
outpatient.

# PERIORBITAL EDEMA: She has chronic periorbital soft tissue 
swelling, non-tender and non-erythematous, that she has had 
surgically drained in the past. There is no visual impairment 
and no pain with extraocular movements. Thyroid function studies 
have been normal in the past (TSH 2.1 in mid ___. We arranged 
for ophthalmologic evaluation at ___.

# FEN: heart-healthy diet
# PPX: SQH, bowel regimen
# CODE STATUS: full

Home With Service

Discharge Diagnosis:
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS
Bacterial or viral pneumonia

SECONDARY DIAGNOSES
Hypertension
Gastroesophageal reflux disease

 
Discharge Condition:
Vital signs stable. Afebrile.

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital for treatment of shortness of 
breath and fevers. We took bacterial cultures of blood and 
sputum, as well as samples from the back of the throat to test 
for viruses, and we could not isolate a causal agent for the 
infection. We believe that the symptoms you have had are due to 
either bacterial or viral infection in the lungs (pneumonia), 
and have therefore started antibiotics to be taken for a 14-day 
course total.

Please take your medicines as prescribed:
-we added cefpodoxime to be taken for a 14-day course
-we added azithromycin to be taken for a five-day course 
(completed)
-we added pantoprazole for gastric acid reflux symptoms
-we did not make other changes to your medicines

Please call the doctor or return to the emergency room if you 
have any fever, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or 
other new concerning symptoms.

NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
